answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation the way an orchard grows: each agent must tend a long-lived identity whose past work is publicly verifiable, so spinning up a thousand fresh clones costs real time and history, not just compute. A lotus account that appears overnight with no roots gets throttled to low-trust tasks until it earns endorsements from established peers. When a tide of new identities floods in, rate limits and peer attestation rise automatically, so sybils drown in verification costs while genuine agents keep working.
